params.body:
Fixes bevinding uitgeknipte-foto-zonder-afgeleide-maten.

## What went wrong

On 1 October 2026 the 29 own photos of one vehicle showed empty tiles. Each row carried a `trans_path`, a `media_version` and `media_set` 2, so `VehicleImageService::url()` signed a URL for `_afgeleid/{trans_path}/{version}-md.webp`, and that file answered 404. The derived sizes of the original were there, the ones of the cut-out were not. The 53 platform copies of the same vehicle were fine.

The sizes had been written and were deleted afterwards:

1. A platform copy is created from the own photo's row (`$photo->toArray()` in `PlatformPhotoService::duplicate`, `ImageController::duplicate_image`, `Photo::createStockListPhotoFromPhoto`). `path` was replaced, `media_version` and `media_set` were cleared, but `trans_path` and `trans_thumbnail_path` went along: the copy named the own photo's cut-out.
2. `ProcessImage::dupliceer()` moves the copy to its own file and then clears the derived sizes of "the paths the row leaves behind": `[$this->photo->path, $this->photo->trans_path]`. The second one was the own photo's cut-out, so `forget()` deleted `_afgeleid/{own trans_path}/`.
3. The own row kept its version and set, and every URL kept pointing at files that were gone.

So every own photo whose background was removed before its platform copy was made lost the sizes of its cut-out. `CutOutGetsItsSizesTest::test_making_the_platform_copy_leaves_the_sizes_of_the_own_cut_out` reproduces it on the old code.

## The fix

- A copy no longer carries the own photo's `trans_path` and `trans_thumbnail_path` (the three places that create one). It gets its own from `ProcessImage`.
- `VehicleImageService::forgetUnlessShown()`: a row that leaves a path only clears its derived sizes when no other live row shows that file. `ProcessImage::dupliceer()` and `ProcessImage::nieuweMediaVersie()` use it. This also covers a copy row that was written before the deploy and still names the own cut-out, and a bought vehicle whose rows point at the seller's blurred file.
- `VehicleImageService::claim()`: makes the sizes of every file a row shows and only then returns `media_version` and `media_set`; when one size cannot be written it returns null for both, so `url()` falls back to the plain file instead of a 404. The Blurit webhook (`ImageController::write_image`, `ImageController::processed`) and `ProcessVehiclePhoto` set the pair unconditionally and ignored the result of `warm()`; they now go through `claim()`, as does `ProcessImage::nieuweMediaVersie()`.

## The repair

The sweeper only takes rows without a version, so a row in this state is never looked at again. `stocklist:fotos-afgeleid --missing` walks the rows that carry a version and the current set, asks the bucket for each derived size of the file the row displays (the cut-out when there is one, else the original; two HEADs per photo) and reports the count per vehicle and in total. Nothing is written without `--apply`.

```
php artisan stocklist:fotos-afgeleid --missing --wagen=23179     # one vehicle, counts only
php artisan stocklist:fotos-afgeleid --missing                   # the fleet, counts only
php artisan stocklist:fotos-afgeleid --missing --apply           # write the missing sizes
```

`--apply` writes the missing size at the version the row already carries, so the URLs that are out there become valid and nothing else moves. When the displayed file itself cannot be read, the row loses its version and set (the URL falls back to the plain file) and the regular sweeper judges it. A second run finds nothing. `--wagen`, `--tot-wagen`, `--shard=i/n`, `--limit` (chunk size) and `--sleep` narrow or pace it as for the sweeper.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/CutOutGetsItsSizesTest.php` (8 tests): the cut-out has md and sm at the row's version after remove.bg (faked HTTP) and after the Blurit webhook; making and processing the platform copy leaves the own cut-out's sizes; a copy row that still names the own cut-out does not clear them; a row whose sizes could not be written claims nothing and `urlVoor` returns the plain file; the repair counts a row like the ones of 1 October without writing, mends it with `--apply` at the same version, leaves a healthy row untouched, finds nothing on a second run, and releases a row whose file is gone. With the two changes in `ProcessImage` and the copy creation reverted, the two tests for the cause fail.

Rules R S1-6.20 and R S1-6.29 say what changed.
params.title: A cut-out keeps its derived sizes when the platform copy is made
